text:
maria: Heads-up — I'm putting together a small CI job to auto-collect GPU traces on our nightly perf runs. Goal: kernel timeline + KV-cache hotspots + batch-size traces so the diff dashboard can surface regressions. Draft below.

maria: CI job (draft):
```yaml
name: nightly-perf-trace
on: schedule
  # run at 03:00 UTC daily
schedule: 
  - cron: '0 3 * * *'
jobs:
  trace-collect:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: run nsys capture
        run: |
          sudo nvidia-smi -q
          export MODEL=redwood-tiny
          ./bin/run_inference --batch-size=16 --seq-len=1024 --steps=50 
          nsys profile --output ${MODEL}-${GITHUB_RUN_ID} --trace=cuda,nvtx --sample=none \n            --capture-range=kernel --capture-range-end=kernel -- 
            ./bin/run_inference --batch-size=16 --seq-len=1024 --steps=50
      - name: upload artifacts
        run: tar -cJf ${MODEL}-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}.tar.xz out/ && aws s3 cp ${MODEL}-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}.tar.xz s3://redwood-perf-traces/nightly/
```

chris: Love this. Quick q: how big are the traces and retention plan? 

maria: Traces ~1.5–3GB compressed per run depending on seq-len. Plan: keep 14 days in hot bucket, then lifecycle to cold for 90d, delete after 120d. We also snapshot a small perfmeta.json for the diff tool.

anita: Can we limit capture window to the hot path only? we should avoid full 60s traces for cost/IO. Also filter out any customer payloads.

lee: +1 to limited windows. Also add NVTX ranges from the runtime so we can attribute kernel choices to high-level ops. We already emit: `NVTX_PUSH("kvcache:lookup")` and `NVTX_PUSH("kvcache:store")` in runtime. The nsys command should include `--trace=nvtx,cuda` so those show up.

maria: Yep runtime emits NVTX. Example capture command we'll standardize on: 
```bash
nsys profile -o ${OUT} --trace=cuda,nvtx --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-begin="runtime:request_start" --capture-range-end="runtime:request_end" --sample=none --cuda-memory-usage off --nvtx-all 
```

ryan: For the diff dashboard we need a `perfmeta.json` with keys: model, commit, batch_size, seq_len, mean_token_latency_ms, top_kernels. Example (stored alongside artifacts):

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-tiny",
  "commit": "a1b2c3d",
  "batch_size": 16,
  "seq_len": 1024,
  "mean_token_latency_ms": 12.8,
  "top_kernels": ["cuda::matmul_fwd", "layernorm_fwd", "kv_cache_lookup"]
}
```

devx: We'll register the artifact in perf-db and attach S3 path and perfmeta. Also add lifecycle policy: auto-delete >120d unless flagged. Consider sampling strategy: run full trace 1/3 nightly to save cost, and lightweight telemetry every night.

chris: How do we detect regressions automatically? We should diff per-kernel P95/P50 across runs and create alerts when any kernel has >15% regression and contributes >5% of tokens.

maria: Agreed. Plan: the nightly job uploads the raw trace + `perfmeta.json` then a downstream job (perf-analyze) runs a lightweight `nsys stats` pass to emit per-kernel aggregates, stores CSV/JSON, and the dashboard compares last 7 runs. If threshold hit, it opens a ticket in #incidents with the diff image.

perf-bot: Dry-run scheduled by @maria for 1799901234. Upload path: s3://redwood-perf-traces/dryrun/1799901234.tar.xz (size 1.9GB).

anita: One more ask — add PII scrubber step before upload: mask input tokens and any logged prompt text.

maria: Will add scrubber and clip trace length to 30s of active runtime per request. Also will add sampling flag `TRACE_SAMPLE_RATE=0.33` by default.

lee: After we have traces, I'll run perfetto on a subset to get kernel flame view and try to isolate KV cache stalls. I've seen KV cache lookups creating micro-bursts that shift kernel scheduling.

chris: Can we also capture hardware counters for a small sample? L2 cache miss rates would be useful for quantization effects. If nsys supports `--events` on our GPUs we should enable it for the 1/3 sampled runs.

maria: Good idea. We'll add `--event=dram_read_transactions,l2_read_transactions` for sampled runs only.

ryan: Next steps?

maria: I'll push a PR for the GH action + perfmeta schema today. After review we'll enable dry-run in staging, then flip to production sampling next week. I'll post the PR link once ready. cc @devx for perf-db registration details.

maria: Thanks — updating now.

chris: Nice. Once this is live we should schedule a 30-min sync to walk through the dashboard flows and alerting thresholds. :thumbsup:
